newsitem.title: USA: HBO to offer HDTV by summer '98 - NYT.
newsitem.headline: HBO to offer HDTV by summer '98 - NYT.

text.p: Home Box Office plans to begin offering digital high-definition television programming by next summer, the New York Times said.
In Wednesday's edition, the Times said HBO's move makes it one of the first by a cable company to adopt the digital high-definition TV format, which also is known as HDTV.

HBO Chairman Jeffrey Bewkes said it was not an attempt to put pressure on broadcasters who, some believe, may use the format to offer four or five channels of standard-definition programming rather than a single HDTV signal.

"The broadcast-spectrum issue may be a part of it for some of the companies, but that's not what is motivating us," Bewkes said. "Customers have come to expect us to be first when new technologies come along, and we think high definition is one of those things."
HBO is owned by Time Warner Inc.
